solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Island man's hiding a posh car

indicators.note: a word that hides something wraps itself round it

parts.note: belonging to a man is his
RR is short for Rolls-Royce, the archetypal posh car

explanation.surface: A man is concealing an expensive car he owns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Island man's' reads as a man from an island, but the island alone is the definition; 'hiding' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Harris is part of the Outer Hebrides, off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Used to find hobby could be a case of work born in purgatory

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for purgatory

parts.note: a torment or ordeal is a hell

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside letters, here W and K

explanation.surface: Taking up a pastime might be a sort of job born in torment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hobby' is not a pastime but a small falcon; falconers tie a bell to the bird to find it. 'in' is the container signal, 'case of' the outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Falconers fasten a small bell to a hunting bird's leg so they can locate it when it is out of sight.

indicators.note: wretched means in a bad state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone swears at a miserable Greek restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'darn' looks like a mild curse, but it is fodder; 'wretched' rearranges DARN TAVERNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranting and raving is shouting angrily, much like swearing or cursing.

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the following word

explanation.surface: A description of the condition someone hopeful is in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' suggests a condition; it is a country, inside asp-IRAN-t.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in the Middle East, and a nation is a state.

clue.text: Diver turns regularly in case coming across shipping hazards

indicators.note: the case letters stretch across the reversed bird, enclosing it
every other letter of the words in case is taken, starting with the first
the bird's name is read in the other direction

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: A diver keeps turning inside a protective case while crossing a busy sea lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes I, C, S from 'in case'; 'turns' gives EBERG from GREBE, which those letters come across.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating masses of ice are a classic danger to vessels at sea, as the Titanic found.

clue.text: A measure of warmth and friendship for Jane, maybe

parts.note: cal is short for calorie, a unit of heat
amity is friendship

explanation.surface: Warmth and friendship offered to a woman called Jane.
explanation.walkthrough: Calamity Jane was a frontierswoman of the American Wild West.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamity was the nickname of Martha Jane Canary, the frontierswoman known as Calamity Jane.

parts.note: pulses are legumes; heads overheated in the sun could jokingly be called cooked noggins, bean being slang for head

explanation.surface: The heartbeat of angry, impetuous people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulses' looks like heartbeats but means legumes; 'bean' is slang for head, so cooked hot heads are a tinned staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Haricots in tomato sauce are pulses, and bean is slang for a head, here one that is hot.

definitions.meaning: a skate or similar flat cartilaginous sea creature
the given name of soul singer ... Charles, with perhaps marking him as one example

explanation.surface: Looking for a fish that suits a man called Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a flat sea creature and the first name of the American singer Ray Charles.

definitions.meaning: slang for informing on accomplices to the police

explanation.surface: An instruction to make music and yell.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminal slang uses both words for betraying accomplices, and the word is also a shrill cry.

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, a round letter, so the word no loses its round letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: It has been a long while without romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective about time but is the verb, to pine; 'loveless' drops O from NO.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to pine or ache for it.

indicators.note: the word for shrinking goes round the word for collar

parts.note: to wane is to shrink or diminish
to collar someone is to nab them

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist goes round the neckline of a candidate for holy orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' looks like a psychiatrist and 'collar' a cleric's, but both are verbs; 'round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A postulant is an aspiring candidate, someone who would like to become something: an aspirant.

clue.text: Listen to story line as a reader

indicators.note: the solver is told to hear the words rather than read them

parts.note: a lie is a story, a fib; a queue is a line of people waiting

explanation.surface: An instruction to hear a plot read out by someone reading.
explanation.walkthrough: LIE + QUEUE said aloud gives the phrase. The definition puns on 'reader': the person reading this clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase compares something with the person addressed, and the person reading the clue is that addressee.

definitions.meaning: to ... a load is to support it
Paddington is the fictional marmalade-loving creature from darkest Peru

explanation.surface: Someone asks who will back Paddington.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the verb of carrying weight; the other is the animal Paddington is, from Michael Bond's books.

clue.text: Woman from Capri, mad on narcissism

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the following run of words

explanation.surface: A woman from Capri who is crazy about self-love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the letters inside capRI MAD ON NArcissism. The narcissism in the surface fits the vain woman the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a vain, temperamental woman, originally the leading female singer in an opera.

indicators.note: the letters are fashioned, shaped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A demand for the frostiest sense of style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of fashion' looks like style but is the anagram signal on ICIEST SENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Essentials and requirements are what one must have, plural nouns like needs.

parts.note: a tuber with eyes planted to grow a crop that will in time become fries

explanation.surface: Someone watching the first course of a plate of fries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyed' looks like watched; it means having eyes, the buds on a tuber. 'starter' is not a first course but where a crop starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubers kept for planting sprout from their eyes and begin the crop that ends up as fries.

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an adder is something that computes sums

explanation.surface: A large computer has trouble with keeping goods in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' looks like keeping goods in stock but is the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A run in tights or hosiery is called a ladder in British English.

definitions.meaning: slang for a term in prison

explanation.surface: An order to lengthen a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to lengthen, and in criminal slang it is also a prison term served.

indicators.note: done in a fantastic, wild way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something produces a wonderfully wholesome beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastically' rearranges GENERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfermented tea from China and Japan is promoted as a wholesome beverage rich in antioxidants.

definitions.meaning: a champion or supporter of a cause
in maths the superscript showing how many times to multiply a number by itself

explanation.surface: A champion who represents authority.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a promoter of an idea, and the index written above a number to show raising to a power.

clue.text: They're used to smooth introduction to sex with Swede

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word sex is taken

parts.note: Anders is a common Swedish man's name

explanation.surface: Racy picture of a Swede smoothing the way into a sexual encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduction to' gives S from 'sex'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanding machines or tools wear surfaces down until they are even and flat.

parts.note: a fashion indifferent to the wearer's gender; and split in two, what students enjoy at university

explanation.surface: A careless way of dressing that students like.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as UNI + SEX, the answer is what students supposedly enjoy; whole, it is clothing made for either gender.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing or hairstyles suitable for both men and women are indifferent to gender.

clue.text: Number 1 in School Close is missing address

indicators.note: the first piece goes inside the shortened school
the close, or end, of the word school is lost

parts.note: taken as written
number one is a childish euphemism for urinating, a pee

explanation.surface: A school's head pupil is absent from the street called School Close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number 1' suggests a head pupil and 'School Close' a street name; 'Close is missing' drops the end of the word, leaving SCH, and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal talk to an audience is an address, as in a public oration.

indicators.note: only parts of the two words, the end of one and the start of the next, are used

parts.note: John and his son Sebastian, who shared a surname and both sailed to the New World, so one name covers both

explanation.surface: Adventurers who went to the north and the south of the Americas.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'both parts' look like north and south; the letters sit across ameri-CA BOT-h. John Cabot and his son Sebastian both explored the New World.
explanation.definitionFit: John and Sebastian, father and son, were both seafaring discoverers who sailed to the New World.

indicators.note: the word for friend goes over the other two pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a hen is a female bird
an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: A friend hides a portent about birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' is the container signal: the friend wraps round the bird and the sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Something remarkable or extraordinary is described as outstanding in this way.

parts.note: livestock fodder such as silage is kept in this tall farm structure

explanation.surface: A shop that keeps food in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like a verb about shelves, but it means livestock; the store holds their feed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower or pit for storing grain or silage feeds farm animals.

clue.text: Style of architecture from Renaissance often represented in capitals

indicators.note: only the capital letters, the initial of each word, stand for the words

explanation.surface: A Renaissance building style is often shown in column tops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitals' suggests tops of columns, fitting 'architecture'; here it means initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded, bushy natural hairstyle is called this, so it is a style of hair.

clue.text: Graceful sweetheart has attachment to foot soldier, perhaps

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E
the foot is attached to the leg
a soldier ant is one kind of the insect

explanation.surface: A lover with a foot-soldier fixation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is the classic crossword device for the centre letter of 'sweet'; 'soldier' is an insect caste, not a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceful and stylish in appearance or movement are near synonyms.

indicators.note: going backwards, so the general's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general

explanation.surface: General support offered on behalf of a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but reverses LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, snakelike creature of rivers and seas is a kind of fish.

clue.text: On which cover is placed in an illegal position

definitions.meaning: in cricket the fielding position called cover lies on this half of the field
in football a player ahead of the ball and defenders is penalised for this

explanation.surface: Something about where insurance cover is put while illegally parked.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover is a cricket fielding position, in front of the batsman on the side away from the legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The off side is the half of a cricket field where cover stands, and a footballer caught too far forward is penalised.

parts.note: something hollow is empty inside
ay (or aye) is an old word meaning always

explanation.surface: A jail lies empty for good.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLLOWAY was a women's prison in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Holloway was a well-known London jail, which held women until it closed in 2016.

parts.note: a stiff undergarment restrains a growing waistline; corporate hints at corporation, slang for a paunch, and at business

explanation.surface: A regulation limiting how big firms can grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporate' points at business, but a corporation is also slang for a pot belly. The word was also the nickname of a 1970s Bank of England curb on bank lending.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight undergarment constrains the body's spread, and the word was used for a curb on banks' lending growth.
